import mir_eval
import numpy as np

# Encode a standard chord label into its numerical representations
root, intervals, bass = mir_eval.chord.encode(
    "C:maj7", reduce_extended_chords=False, strict_bass_intervals=False
)

# Verify the absolute root (C = 0)
assert root == 0, f"Expected root 0 for 'C', got {root}"

# Verify the bass note relative to the root (root position = 0)
assert bass == 0, f"Expected bass 0 for root position, got {bass}"

# Verify the 12-dimensional relative semitone bitmap for a major 7th chord
# (root=0, major 3rd=4, perfect 5th=7, major 7th=11)
assert intervals.shape == (12,), f"Expected 12-dim bitmap, got shape {intervals.shape}"
assert np.sum(intervals) == 4, f"Expected 4 active semitones, got {np.sum(intervals)}"
assert intervals[0] == 1 and intervals[4] == 1 and intervals[7] == 1 and intervals[11] == 1, \
    f"Incorrect intervals for maj7: {intervals}"

print(f"__CHECK__ encode root={root}, active_intervals={np.sum(intervals)}, bass={bass}")
